summary: Selection sort repeatedly finds the smallest unsorted value and swaps it into place. Insertion sort takes each value and shifts larger values right until it fits.
notes: [items[i], items[smallest]] = [items[smallest], items[i]]; swaps two values without a temporary variable.
The outer loop of selection sort runs items.length - 1 times. The last value is already in place.
Both functions change the array in place. They do not make a new array.
pitfall: Starting a line with [ right after a line with no semicolon, like let x = 5 then [a, b] = [b, a], makes JavaScript read both lines as one statement and the swap does not happen. End the line before a destructuring swap with a semicolon.
contrast: JavaScript swaps in one line with array destructuring, [a, b] = [b, a], close to Python's a, b = b, a. Java needs a temporary variable.
